title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
abstract: arXiv:2610.40649v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The Neural Thickets hypothesis posits that pretrained language models lie in dense neighborhoods of task-specific experts in weight space, which random Gaussian perturbations can uncover. We reproduce the reported gains, but show that they do not require this geometric explanation. Perturbing a single decoder block already recovers much of the improvement, while keeping the model entirely frozen and adding a random bias to its output logits matches or exceeds full-weight perturbations on most reasoning tasks. This suggests an alternative explanation based on output diversity, validation-based selection, and voting. We formalize this view as Perturb-Select-Vote (PSV), a general procedure that generates perturbed predictors, selects high-performing members on a small validation set, and aggregates their predictions. translated_title: 重新思考神经灌木丛：无需权重扰动
translated_abstract: 神经灌木丛假说认为，预训练语言模型在权重空间中位于特定任务专家的密集邻域内，而随机高斯扰动能够揭示这些专家。我们复现了此前报告的性能提升，但证明这些提升并不需要这种几何解释。仅扰动单个解码器块就能恢复大部分改进；而在完全冻结模型的情况下，仅在其输出logits上添加随机偏置，就能在大多数推理任务上匹敌甚至超越全权重扰动。这提示了一种基于输出多样性、基于验证集的选择与投票的替代解释。我们将这一观点形式化为“扰动-选择-投票”（Perturb-Select-Vote, PSV），这是一种通用流程：生成扰动预测器，在小验证集上筛选表现优异的成员，并聚合它们的预测结果。这一解释将神经灌木丛与已有的推理时方法（包括采样、自洽性等）联系起来。
tldr: 该研究证明神经灌木丛的性能提升无需依赖权重扰动的几何解释——完全冻结模型、仅在输出logits上添加随机偏置即可达到相同甚至更好的效果，并将该现象重新形式化为“扰动-选择-投票”（PSV）这一推理时方法。
en_tdlr: This work shows that Neural Thickets gains do not require the geometric weight-perturbation explanation—simply freezing the model and adding random biases to output logits matches or exceeds full perturbations—recasting the phenomenon as a Perturb-Select-Vote (PSV) inference-time procedure.
